newsitem.title: DENMARK: Den Danske sees stable Danish crown and repo rate.
newsitem.headline: Den Danske sees stable Danish crown and repo rate.

text.p: Den Danske Bank said on Wednesday that it expected central bank interest rates and the crown currency to remain stable over the next 12 months.

In its latest economic forecast Den Danske said that stability remained the central bank's main priority and it was therefore hard to imagine that it would alter the repo rate as long as the currency market remained calm.
"We therefore expect that the gap (between the Danish and German repo rates) will be 50 basis points in both three months and 12 months time," the survey said.

The Danish rate has been unchanged at 3.50 percent since it was cut from 3.70 in August last year. The central bank steers money market rates and liquidity through repos and CDs, which also pay 3.50 percent.

Den Danske saw the strengthening Danish economy shrinking the yield gap between the incoming benchmark seven percent 2007 Danish government bond and the German bund to around 50 basis points over the coming three months.
At midday on Wednesday the gap was 67 basis points and the crown was steady at 3.8072 to the mark.
The crown generally stays close to its ERM central rate of 3.8144 to the mark although it has weakened against other currencies, such as the dollar and sterling.
